text: Which statement best describes an AWS Availability Zone?

options.text: A geographic area that contains several AWS Regions
A site that Amazon CloudFront uses to cache content close to users
One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity within an AWS Region
AWS hardware installed in a customer's own data center

explanation: An Availability Zone is one or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, and it sits inside a Region. A Region contains AZs (not the other way round), a CloudFront cache site is an edge location, and hardware in a customer data center is AWS Outposts.

text: A healthcare company in Europe must keep patient records inside the European Union to comply with a regulation. What should be the company's FIRST consideration when it chooses an AWS Region for this workload?

options.text: The lowest price per instance-hour among all Regions
The Region with the newest AWS services
The Region closest to the company's software developers
Compliance with the data residency requirement

explanation: Legal and regulatory requirements come first, because a Region outside the EU cannot be used no matter how cheap or feature-rich it is. Price, service availability, and latency are weighed only among the Regions that meet the compliance requirement.

text: A company is selecting an AWS Region for a new customer-facing application and has no regulatory restrictions on data location. Which factors should the company evaluate? (Choose two.)

options.text: Latency between the Region and the application's end users
The number of IAM users in the company's AWS account
Pricing of the required services in the Region
The AWS Support plan the company has purchased
The total size of the company's existing Amazon S3 buckets

explanation: Region selection weighs compliance, latency to users, cost, and service availability; prices for the same service differ between Regions. IAM is a global service and a Support plan applies to the whole account, so neither changes from one Region to another.

text: An online learning platform stores video lessons in an Amazon S3 bucket in one AWS Region. Students on other continents complain that videos load slowly. Which AWS service will improve load times by caching the videos closer to the students?

options.text: AWS Global Accelerator
Amazon CloudFront
AWS Outposts
Amazon Route 53

explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a content delivery network that caches content such as videos at edge locations near viewers and can use an S3 bucket as its origin. AWS Global Accelerator also uses edge locations but improves the network path to endpoints rather than caching content.

text: A multiplayer game uses UDP traffic. The company needs fixed static IP addresses that send players over the AWS global network to the nearest healthy endpoint in one of several AWS Regions. Which AWS service meets these requirements?

options.text: Amazon CloudFront
AWS Local Zones
AWS Global Accelerator
AWS Wavelength

explanation: AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and routes TCP or UDP traffic over the AWS global network to healthy endpoints in one or more Regions. CloudFront is aimed at caching and accelerating web content, not at giving static IP entry points for UDP games.

text: A media company has video editors working from several studios across one large city. The editing application needs single-digit millisecond latency to the editors, and the company does not want to install or host any hardware itself. Which AWS infrastructure option should the company use?

options.text: AWS Local Zones
AWS Outposts
Amazon CloudFront edge locations
An additional Availability Zone in a distant Region

explanation: Local Zones place compute, storage, and other services close to large population and industry centers for low-latency workloads such as media production. Outposts would also be low latency, but it requires AWS hardware to be installed at the customer's own site, which the company wants to avoid.

text: A developer wants users of a mobile app on a 5G network to reach the app's backend with ultra-low latency. Which AWS service places AWS compute and storage at the edge of telecommunications providers' networks?

options.text: AWS Local Zones
AWS Outposts
AWS Direct Connect
AWS Wavelength

explanation: AWS Wavelength deploys AWS compute and storage inside telecommunications providers' data centers at the edge of their networks, for low latency to mobile devices. Local Zones are placed near large cities but are not inside the mobile carriers' networks.

text: A company runs its web application on Amazon EC2 instances that are all in a single Availability Zone. Which changes will keep the application available if that Availability Zone fails? (Choose two.)

options.text: Change the existing instances to a larger instance type
Run instances in at least two Availability Zones in the Region
Add more instances in the same Availability Zone
Use a load balancer to distribute traffic across instances in multiple Availability Zones
Configure Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling to keep a fixed number of instances in the current Availability Zone

explanation: Availability Zones do not share single points of failure, so running instances in several AZs behind a load balancer keeps the application up when one AZ fails. Larger instances, extra instances, or an Auto Scaling group that stays in the same AZ would all fail together with that AZ.

text: Which statement about AWS Regions is correct?

options.text: Every AWS Region contains exactly two Availability Zones
Data stored by a regional service stays in its Region unless the customer copies or replicates it elsewhere
Every AWS service is available in every Region
An edge location is a smaller type of AWS Region

explanation: For regional services, resources and data created in one Region do not exist in another Region unless the customer explicitly copies or replicates them, which supports data residency; AWS moves content only as needed to provide the services the customer chose or to comply with law. Public Regions are built with at least three Availability Zones, and service availability differs between Regions.

text: Which are valid reasons for a company to deploy a workload in more than one AWS Region? (Choose two.)

options.text: To get more Availability Zones inside a single Region
To reduce latency between components that must communicate synchronously
To recover from a disaster that makes an entire Region unavailable
To avoid having to replicate data between locations
To give lower latency to users on different continents

explanation: Multiple Regions support disaster recovery and business continuity, lower latency for users around the world, and data sovereignty. Spreading tightly linked components across Regions adds latency between them, and a multi-Region design needs more data replication, not less.
